title: Temporal-segmentation KV allocator with live thin-compaction and hotspot reshuffle
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: High fragmentation in the KV cache under mixed short-chat and long-document workloads leads to elevated GPU memory footprints and uneven eviction behavior. Continuous batching amplifies fragmentation because requests interleave allocations of varying lifetimes, and current compaction strategies require full-page rewrites which cause latency spikes or are run infrequently, allowing fragmentation to accumulate.

Proposal: Implement a temporal-segmentation allocator: divide the large KV region into age-buckets (hot, mid, cold) and allocate entries into the youngest feasible bucket. Introduce a live 'thin compaction' process that migrates compact metadata (pointer tables and small headers) and performs scatter-gather relocation of only the minimum physical slices necessary to consolidate free spans. Complement with a hotspot reshuffle policy that promotes high-hit entries into a compact hot lane to improve cache hit locality. The approach prioritizes minimal copy bandwidth, bounded background work, and fine-grained control to avoid impacting P99 latency during continuous batching.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end integration with KV allocator and runtime scheduler merged to main; 2) Compaction can run concurrently with inference without violating p95 latency SLOs; 3) Fragmentation ratio decreases by >= 20% on mixed chat/long-doc synthetic workloads; 4) Peak GPU memory reduced by >= 12% for long-context tests; 5) New KV telemetry exposed and visible in Console (fragmentation_ratio, hotset_hit_rate, compaction_cpu_ms, compaction_gpu_ms); 6) Canary rollout plan executed with telemetry checks and rollback on regressions.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: 
- Age buckets: choose 3 tiers initially (hot: <1s lifetime, mid: 1s-1m, cold: >1m) configurable via runtime flags.
- Thin compaction: perform pointer-level relocation first; only copy token payloads when anchored spans permit contiguous consolidation. This reduces PCIe/GPU copy traffic.
- Scatter-gather relocation kernel: leverage existing CUDA/rocm memcpy primitives and peer-to-peer copy where available. Use an adaptive batch-size so we don't saturate streaming multiprocessors during online compaction.
- Hotspot reshuffle: maintain a lightweight LRU-ish bloom-weighted counter to identify high-hit keys; background worker moves these keys to hot lane during low-util windows.
- Safety: compaction operates with write barriers; in-flight requests consult a reloc map to find the current location. We will reuse the existing indirection layer introduced in runtime-1.18.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full-page rewrite vs thin compaction: full-page offers maximum defrag at cost of large copy windows and latency spikes; thin compaction is lower bandwidth but leaves some fragmentation that must be periodically trimmed. We chose thin compaction to preserve tail-latency.
- Number of buckets: more buckets reduce cross-tenure churn but increase allocator complexity; starting with 3 keeps implementation tractable.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for allocator invariants (no leaks, relocation atomicity), integration tests with synthetic continuous-batching harness (mixed short+long sequences), and end-to-end perf tests on dedicated cluster. Key tests: 
- Synthetic chat-heavy workload (90% short sequences)
- Long-context workload (95th percentile tokens > 64k total)
- Mixed workload (50/50) with bursty arrival patterns to exercise scatter-gather.
- Fault injection: worker kills during compaction to verify recovery and reloc-map correctness.
- Nightly regression job comparing fragmentation_ratio and peak_memory to baseline.

Benchmarks so far (internal): 
- Mixed workload run (48h): fragmentation_ratio baseline 0.42 -> after prototype passes 0.31 (26% drop).
- Peak GPU memory: baseline 74GB -> prototype 64GB (13.5% reduction).
- Observed transient p99 increase of ~3.1% during aggressive compaction passes; mitigated via smaller passes and accelerated backoff.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime-1.19 config; 2) Canary: enable for 5 dedicated pods on non-production clusters for 72h and collect telemetry; 3) Canary: enable 10% of dedicated customer traffic for 72h with auto-rollbacks on SLO regressions; 4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with monitoring checks at each step.
Rollback criteria: >1% absolute increase in p95 latency, fragmentation_ratio increases, or any customer-critical error surfaced by runtime checks.
